class.name: InputBufferSystem
class.brief_description: Decouples OS and Engine input from the deterministic ECS simulation.
class.description: [InputBufferSystem] is a middleware layer designed for gameplay sensitivity and determinism. it collects events from Godot's [Input] singleton and buffers them into entity-level [InputComponent]s. This decoupling is essential for simulation features like [b]Input Replay[/b], [b]Network Rollback[/b], and "Glitch Horror" mechanics where the game might procedurally override or corrupt player controls. [b]Feature Set:[/b] - [b]Action Remapping:[/b] Dynamically swap player controls during runtime for different gameplay modes (e.g., vehicle vs. on-foot). - [b]Input Locking:[/b] Global control inhibition for cutscenes or menu interaction. - [b]Low-Latency Polling:[/b] Synchronized with the fixed physics tick for frame-perfect character control.

method.name: lock_player_input
method.description: If [param locked] is [code]true[/code], all entities with an [InputComponent] will receive static "neutral" values, effectively ignoring physical hardware input.

method.name: remap_action
method.description: Maps a virtual name (used by your ECS systems) to a physical Godot Input Action (defined in the Project Input Map).

method.name: process_input_buffer
method.description: Captures the current state of physical input devices and pushes them into the corresponding ECS components.
